business_problem: Hematogenix's fixed on-premises compute infrastructure bottlenecked its AI initiatives and could not support large training runs across its proprietary multimodal oncology dataset while meeting strict data-governance requirements.
solution_summary: Hematogenix moved its proprietary multimodal oncology data and AI research from fixed on-premises infrastructure to Google Cloud, where resources can be provisioned on demand and released when jobs finish. Engineers use Workbench to curate datasets in BigQuery and run small experiments, including genetic-mutation prediction, before expanding validated work into production pipelines. Compute Engine supplies scalable compute, while Google Kubernetes Engine supports resource provisioning and parallel project execution. The source also names Gemini and Model Garden on the Gemini platform among the data and AI tools used, but does not detail their individual roles. Capacity grew from 16 on-premises GPUs to hundreds on demand; HIPAA, GDPR, and ISO compliance were among the reasons for the move. The page does not specify data ingestion or model-serving topology.
